chapter_theme: Songs at Gnanamalai (ஞானமலை): the poet rejects the diseased, bargaining women of the street who stand beside gamblers and killers, and, mocked by wife, town and kin, asks at death for the feet he was once given, the feet that melted him and gave the experience of yoga.
structure_note: Two songs: 609 a courtesan catalogue, 610 a song of public shame that recalls an earlier gift of the feet at this shrine.

609.reading: The poet lists gamblers and killers and women greedy for money, filthy, pallid and blue-faced, aching with colic and rheumatism, sinful and slanderous, who boast in the street, call 'come', name their price by the measure and the pot and jut their chins in pride, and asks whether relationship with them can be right. The praise names the vel that dried the seven seas to mire while Vedic sages, children, women and Brahmins cried out, the son of Sivakami and Abhirami, and Murugan at Gnanamalai with the daughter of Narayana.
609.nuance: சூது கொலைகாரர் ஆசைபண மாதர் sets gamblers, killers and money-loving women in one list, and the women's diseases (சோகை, சூலை, வாதம்) are named as warning. நாழி தாழி விலை கூறி: they price themselves like grain or a pot of goods. நாரண சுவாமி ஈனும் மகள் is the tradition that Murugan's consorts are Vishnu's daughters.

610.reading: The poet describes how his wife, the town and the world's women laugh at him, his father and kin are troubled, and everyone babbles abuse, and how his mind's darkness grows until he asks 'is this the welfare I gained by taking a body?'; he asks that when his life leaves the body Murugan come near and give the feet he gave before. The praise names the vel that blazed in battle against the demons with drums, veena and Vedas sounding, the feet that melted his mind and gave the experience of yoga, Uma's son, and Murugan at Gnanamalai with the hunter girl and Indra's daughter.
610.nuance: The shame is told as an ever-widening circle: wife, town, women, father, kin, everyone (அனைவரும் இழிப்ப). முன் அளித்த பாதம் and எனை மனம் உருக்கி யோக அநுபுதி அளித்த பாத point back to a gift of the feet already received, which tradition places at Gnanamalai. நாயன் உளமது சலிப்ப, 'the lord's heart troubled', is unclear: the lord may be the poet's master or the Lord himself.

links.note: The Kural names double-hearted women, liquor and dice as the company of those whom fortune has left; 609 opens its list with gamblers and money-loving women side by side and adds disease.
